submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on the predicate token that sets up a stance or evidential frame toward a coming proposition or infinitive: attitude/epistemic verbs and adjectives (' believed', ' hoped', ' suspect', ' sure', ' willing', ' convinced'), evidential verbs only when the subject is a result/evidence noun ('Analysis/The results showed', 'The study found', 'The evidence suggests', but not 'The man showed'), the copula after abstract framing subjects ('The result was', 'There was'), and modal clitics ('It'd', 'It'll'); it also fires on the final suffix piece of tokenizer-split adverbs ('doub|ly', 'defin|et|ly', 'hop|efully', 'eas|ily'). Ordinary content words, concrete-subject verbs ('He bought', 'The man showed'), whole-word adverbs (' quickly', ' very') and the first token of a prompt stay near zero (<0.1 of max), so there is no floor on plain text.
